transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I’m here because things at work have gotten really uncomfortable, and I don’t think people are taking me seriously when I try to explain it. I’m a transportation inspector, and ever since I got that county safety award, certain people at work have been acting different. Not openly, not in a way where you could just point to one thing and say, “There, that’s it,” but it’s there.

They’ve been twisting my inspection reports, asking these pointed questions about budgets and procedures like they’re trying to make me look like I’m doing something crooked or irresponsible. And I’m careful with my reports—I know what I write, I know how I document things. But then it comes back like they’re reading it in the worst possible way on purpose.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, normal oversight, nothing personal, but I don’t buy that. I mean, I can tell when something is routine and when people are lining things up to discredit me. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to damage my reputation after that award made me more visible. That’s really why I came in—because everyone keeps acting like I’m overreacting, but I know what I’m seeing.
Do you think these people at work are specifically targeting you for a reason that's unique to you?

Yes. I mean, that’s what it feels like. It’s not just random office stuff or people being strict with paperwork. It started after I got that county safety award, and I think that made me stand out more than some people liked.

Since then, certain people have been going over my inspection reports like they’re hunting for something, twisting what I wrote, asking these budget questions in this pointed way—like they’re trying to imply I’m careless or maybe doing something shady. And I’m not. I know how I do my job.

My supervisor keeps telling me it’s normal review, normal procedure, but it doesn’t feel normal to me. It feels coordinated, like they’re building a case to make me look crooked or discredit me because I got recognized. So yes, I do think it’s aimed at me specifically.
Do you think there's any possibility that you might be misinterpreting the actions of your coworkers?

I mean… I suppose anyone can misread a situation once in a while, I’m not saying I’m perfect. But this isn’t just one comment or one email I took the wrong way. It’s been a pattern.

Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people started treating my work differently. My inspection reports get picked apart, but not in a normal “let’s clarify this” kind of way. It’s like they’re looking for something to twist. Then they ask these budget questions with this tone, like they’re trying to suggest I’m irresponsible or doing something crooked, when I know exactly how I wrote those reports and why.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just routine review, normal oversight, but I can tell the difference. I’ve been doing this job long enough to know when someone is checking paperwork versus when people are lining things up to make you look bad. So… could I be misinterpreting one little thing? Maybe. But the whole thing? No, I don’t think so. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me because that award put a spotlight on me.
Do you think the people at work are plotting against you in secret?

Plotting… I mean, I don’t know if they’re sitting in some back room with a written plan or anything like that. I’m not trying to make it sound dramatic. But yes, I do think there’s something going on that they’re not saying openly.

Because ever since that county safety award, the way certain people handle my work changed. My inspection reports are being picked through like they’re trying to find a weak spot, and then they ask these budget questions in a way that feels loaded, like they’re trying to make me look careless or crooked. It’s not just normal clarification. I’ve had normal reviews before. This feels different.

And when my supervisor says, “Oh, it’s just routine oversight,” that almost makes it worse, because it feels like everyone is pretending it’s normal when it isn’t. I can tell there’s coordination in it. Maybe not everyone is involved, but certain people, yes. It feels like they’re trying to discredit me because that award put attention on me.
Do you think these people at work are able to control your life or actions in any way?

Control my life or actions? No, I don’t think I’d put it that way. I mean, they can affect things at work, sure — like if they keep questioning my reports or making me defend every little budget detail, that can make my day harder, and it can put pressure on me. It can make me second-guess how I write things because I know they’re going to be looking for something.

But control me, like make me do things or run my life? No. I still decide what I do. I still go to work, do my inspections, write my reports the way they’re supposed to be written. They might be trying to box me in or make me look bad, but I wouldn’t say they can control my actions. That sounds stronger than what I mean.
Do you believe that there is a conspiracy against you at work?

A conspiracy… I know that word sounds big, and I don’t want to sound like I’m saying everyone in the building is involved or that there’s some formal secret meeting. But if you mean, do I think certain people are coordinating against me? Yes, I do.

That’s honestly why I’m here, because ever since I got that county safety award, things changed at work. My inspection reports started getting treated differently. Not normal corrections, not just “can you clarify this section,” but picked apart in a way that feels like they’re trying to find something they can twist. And then the budget questions started coming up with this pointed tone, like they’re trying to imply I’m careless or maybe doing something dishonest, when I know I’m not.

My supervisor keeps calling it routine review, like I’m supposed to just accept that explanation, but I’ve been doing this job long enough to know the difference between normal oversight and people lining things up to make someone look bad. So… conspiracy may be a strong word, but yes, I believe there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me at work.
Do you think this situation at work is the only place where people are against you, or do you feel like you're being targeted in other areas of your life as well?

It’s mostly work. I mean, that’s where I notice it, that’s where the pattern is. I’m not saying strangers on the street are involved or that my whole life is being followed or anything like that. It’s really tied to the job.

Ever since that county safety award, certain people at work just started treating me differently. My inspection reports get pulled apart like they’re looking for something they can use, not just checking them normally. And the budget questions — those feel pointed, like they’re trying to make me look careless or crooked somehow. That’s the part that bothers me, because I know what normal review feels like. I’ve been through normal review.

So when my supervisor says it’s just routine, I don’t buy that completely. It feels coordinated, like there are people there trying to discredit me. But outside of work? No, I haven’t really seen it in other areas the same way. It’s the workplace situation that feels targeted.
Do you think the people at work who you believe are against you are acting alone or if they have support from someone higher up in the organization?

I don’t think it’s just one person acting completely alone, no. I can’t prove there’s someone at the very top signing off on it or anything like that, but it feels like there’s support somewhere above the people doing it, or at least they know they won’t be stopped.

Because if it were just one coworker being jealous or difficult, fine, that would be one thing. But the way my inspection reports started getting twisted after I got that county safety award — not just corrected, but picked apart like they’re looking for something to use against me — and then these budget questions started coming at me in this pointed way, like they’re trying to make me look careless or crooked… that doesn’t feel like one person just having a bad attitude.

And my supervisor keeps saying it’s normal review, routine oversight, all that. But I’ve been there long enough to know what normal review looks like. This feels coordinated. Maybe he’s involved, maybe he’s covering for them, or maybe someone above him is letting it happen. I don’t know exactly how high it goes, but I do think there’s some kind of backing or agreement behind it. They’re trying to discredit me, and it doesn’t feel like they’d be that comfortable doing it unless they had support.
How much distress or anxiety do you feel as a result of what you believe is happening to you at work?

It’s… it’s a lot. I don’t know how to put a number on it exactly, but it weighs on me more than I’d like to admit.

I try to keep it contained because I still have to go in, do the inspections, write the reports, answer questions like a professional. I’m not falling apart in front of people or anything. But inside, yeah, I feel tense. Especially before meetings or when I know one of my reports is being reviewed. I start thinking, “Okay, what are they going to pull out this time? What sentence are they going to twist? What budget line are they going to act suspicious about?” And that makes it hard to just relax and do the job the way I used to.

It’s frustrating too, because I earned that award. I did good work. And now instead of feeling proud of it, I’m sitting there second-guessing how people are going to use things against me. So I’d say the anxiety is moderate, maybe more on some days. It’s not like I can’t function, but it’s definitely affecting me.
If someone were to provide you with clear evidence that your coworkers are not plotting against you, would you be able to consider that you might be misinterpreting their actions?

I mean… if it was actually clear evidence, I’d look at it. I’m not trying to be unreasonable just for the sake of it. I know how that can sound, like I’ve made up my mind and nothing could change it, but that’s not how I see myself.

The problem is, when my supervisor says, “It’s just normal review,” that doesn’t feel like evidence to me. That feels like an explanation that’s too neat. Because I know what normal review looks like. I’ve been doing this work long enough to know when someone is just checking a report versus when they’re picking it apart, looking for one sentence they can twist. And with the budget questions too — the way they’re asked, the timing, the tone — it feels pointed, like they’re trying to make me look careless or even crooked.

So, yes, if somebody could really show me, not just tell me, that there’s no coordinated effort to discredit me, I’d try to consider it. I’m not saying I’d instantly relax and forget everything, because this has been going on since after that county safety award, and it’s hard to ignore the pattern once you’ve seen it. But I’d consider it if it was solid.

I just haven’t seen that kind of proof. What I’ve seen is people acting differently, my inspection reports being twisted, and then everyone acting like I’m supposed to accept it as routine. That’s the part I can’t just brush off.
Do you think your coworkers' actions are the result of their own initiative or if someone or something else is influencing them to behave this way?

I don’t think it’s just them waking up one day and all separately deciding to act that way. That’s the part that bothers me. If it were one coworker making little comments or being jealous because I got the county safety award, I could understand that. People get petty. But this feels more organized than that.

Ever since that award, certain people at work started treating my inspection reports differently. Not just normal corrections, not just “fix this section” or “clarify that note.” It’s like they’re looking for phrases they can twist, or places where they can make it seem like I missed something. And then the budget questions started coming in this pointed way, like they’re trying to suggest I’m careless or crooked somehow. That’s not a coincidence to me.

So whether someone is directly telling them, “Go after him,” or whether they just know they have permission to do it, I can’t say exactly. I don’t have a recording or an email where someone spells it out. But I can tell when something is coordinated. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I know what normal review looks like. This is different.

So yes, I think something or someone is influencing it, or at least allowing it. I don’t think they’d be this comfortable trying to discredit me if they were completely on their own.
Do you think the situation at work is the result of your own actions or something beyond your control?

I don’t think it’s because of something I did wrong, if that’s what you mean. I mean, I did my job. I did the inspections, wrote the reports the way I’m supposed to, followed the process. And then after I got that county safety award, suddenly certain people started acting different around my work.

So to me, this feels mostly beyond my control. I can control how carefully I write a report, or how I answer a budget question, or whether I stay professional in a meeting. I can do all that. But I can’t control people deciding to twist what I wrote, or asking questions in this pointed way like they’re trying to make me look crooked. That’s the part that makes it so frustrating, because I feel like I’m being put in a position where no matter how careful I am, they can still find some sentence or some number and turn it into something suspicious.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s normal review, and I hear that, but I know what normal review looks like. This doesn’t feel like that. It feels coordinated, like certain people are trying to discredit me, and I didn’t start that. I didn’t ask for it. The only thing I did was good work and get recognized for it. So no, I don’t really see it as coming from my own actions, except maybe that the award put attention on me. But the rest of it — the twisting, the budget questions, the way they’re treating my reports — that feels like something being done to me.
Do you think the situation at work is real or could it be a product of your own imagination?

I know you’re asking if it could be in my head, and I’ve tried to ask myself that, because I don’t want to be the guy who reads into every little thing. But honestly, no, it feels real to me. It doesn’t feel like something I just imagined out of nowhere.

I’m here because ever since that county safety award, things changed at work. Certain people started going through my inspection reports differently, not just correcting normal mistakes but twisting things, pulling out lines like they were trying to make me look bad. And then the budget questions started coming in this pointed way, like they were trying to make it seem like I was careless or crooked. That’s not just a feeling I woke up with. It’s based on what I’ve been seeing and hearing.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s normal review, and I understand that’s what he says, but I know what normal review looks like. I’ve been doing this job long enough to know the difference between someone checking your work and someone building a case against you. And this feels coordinated. It feels like certain people are trying to discredit me.

So could someone tell me it’s my imagination? Sure, they can say that. But from where I’m standing, it’s real. I don’t think I’m making it up.
Have you felt like you're being targeted at work consistently since the county safety award, or have there been times when you felt like everything was back to normal?

It’s been pretty consistent, yeah. I mean, there might be an odd day here or there where nobody says anything directly, or things are quieter, but I wouldn’t say it ever really went back to normal. Not the way it was before.

This has been going on for about a year now, basically ever since I got recognized for that county safety initiative. That’s when I noticed the shift. Before that, work had its usual frustrations, like any job, but I didn’t feel like people were watching for a way to turn things against me. After the award, it was like the tone changed, and it never really changed back.

So if you’re asking whether there were stretches where I thought, “Okay, maybe it’s over, everything’s fine again,” not really. There have been calmer periods, maybe, but underneath it I still feel like I’m being targeted.
Do you think the people at work who are supposedly against you could be acting without realizing the impact of their actions on you?

I mean… I’ve tried to give them that benefit of the doubt, honestly. Like, maybe someone asks one budget question a certain way and they don’t realize how it sounds, or maybe someone edits a report and doesn’t understand that it comes across like they’re implying I did something wrong. I can accept that once or twice.

But with this, it’s hard for me to believe they don’t know what they’re doing. Ever since that county safety award, certain people have been going through my inspection reports and pulling things out in a way that makes me look careless or dishonest. And the budget questions aren’t just normal questions, they’re pointed, like they already have an idea they’re trying to prove. That doesn’t feel accidental to me.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, and I hear him, but I know what normal review looks like. This feels more coordinated than that. So could one person here or there not realize the impact? Maybe. But overall, no, I think they know. I think they’re trying to discredit me, and that’s what bothers me so much.
Do you think the actions of your coworkers could be explained by anything other than a deliberate attempt to discredit you?

I’ve tried to think of other explanations, because I know if I just say, “They’re all out to get me,” it sounds extreme. So yes, I’ve asked myself, could it just be regular oversight? Could it be that after the county safety award more eyes were on my work, or maybe the department got stricter about reports and budgets in general? I’ve thought about that.

But when I look at the way it’s actually happening, it doesn’t add up as just normal review. It’s not like they’re simply saying, “Hey, fix this section,” or “We need clarification here.” It’s the way certain lines in my inspection reports get pulled out and turned around, like they’re trying to imply I cut corners or didn’t do my job right. And the budget questions, too — they don’t feel like honest questions. They feel loaded, like someone is trying to make it look like I was being careless with money or like I’m crooked somehow.

My supervisor keeps telling me it’s just standard review, and I hear him say that, but I know the difference. I’ve been doing this work long enough to know what normal checking looks like. This feels coordinated. It feels like certain people decided after that award that I needed to be knocked down or discredited.

So, could there be some other explanation for one thing here or one comment there? Maybe. I’m not saying every single thing is proof. But taken together, no, I really don’t think this is accidental. From what I’m seeing, it feels deliberate.
Do you feel like you're more important or special than others because of your work or the award you received?

No, I don’t think I’m more important than other people. I mean, I was proud of the award, sure. Anybody would be, I think, if they put time into something and it got recognized. It felt good to have the safety work taken seriously, because a lot of that stuff is tedious and people only notice it when something goes wrong.

But I don’t see it like I’m above everyone else or special in some grand way. I still do the same job, still have to show up, still have paperwork, inspections, the same responsibilities. The award didn’t make me better than anybody.

If anything, I think maybe other people reacted differently to it than I did. I saw it as recognition for doing my work right. That’s all. I’m not walking around thinking I’m some big shot. I just don’t think being recognized should make people treat me like I did something wrong.
Have you ever had a period where you felt like the targeting at work stopped or significantly decreased?

Not really, no. I mean, there have been days or maybe a week here and there where it seemed quieter, where nobody said anything directly or there wasn’t some new question about a report or a budget line. But I wouldn’t say it stopped. It’s more like it goes under the surface for a bit and then comes back up again.

This has been going on for about a year now, really since I got recognized for that county safety initiative. That’s when I noticed the shift. Before that, work had normal disagreements, normal corrections, normal back-and-forth. After the recognition, it started feeling like certain people were watching for ways to pick apart what I did.

So if you mean, has there been a real break where I thought, “Okay, this is over, they’ve moved on,” no. I haven’t felt that. It might get less obvious sometimes, but I still feel like it’s there.
Do you think your belief that coworkers are targeting you is something that you might be able to reconsider if presented with evidence to the contrary?

I mean… in theory, yes, I’d like to think I could reconsider something if there was real evidence. I’m not trying to be unreasonable just for the sake of it. If somebody could actually show me, clearly, that the way my reports are being pulled apart and the budget questions are being asked is just normal procedure, and that it’s happening to everyone the same way, then I’d have to look at that.

But the problem is, that’s not what it feels like from where I’m sitting. Ever since that county safety award, it’s been like certain people at work started looking at me differently. My inspection reports get picked through in a way that feels like they’re twisting the wording, like they’re trying to make it sound like I missed something or cut corners. And the budget questions aren’t just ordinary “can you clarify this” questions. They come across pointed, like they’re trying to make me look careless or even crooked.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, and I understand that’s what he says. But I know what normal review looks like. I’ve had my work checked before. This feels coordinated, like it’s not just one misunderstanding or one person having a bad day. It’s the pattern of it.

So… yes, if there was evidence, I’d listen. But it would have to be real evidence, not just somebody telling me, “You’re taking it the wrong way.” Because from what I’ve seen, I don’t think I am.
Do you believe that the actions against you at work are part of a larger plot to harm you outside of work as well?

I wouldn’t say I know it goes outside of work, not in some clear way. I don’t have, like, proof that someone is following me home or anything like that. What I’m here about is mostly work — what’s been happening there since that county safety award.

It’s the way certain people started twisting my inspection reports, picking apart wording like they’re trying to make it seem like I missed something or did something improper. And then the budget questions… they’re not just regular questions. They feel pointed, like they’re trying to make me look careless or crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I’ve been through normal review before, and this doesn’t feel like that.

So, a larger plot outside of work? I don’t know that I’d put it that way. But at work, yes, I do think there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me. That’s the part I can’t just ignore.
